best_for: Makers, students and teachers who program Arduino and compatible boards from a desktop, and who want libraries and board packages installed from menus instead of by hand.
description:
Arduino IDE is the desktop editor from Arduino SA for writing programs, called sketches, and loading them onto Arduino boards. Arduino also offers a command-line tool, a PLC IDE and a MicroPython editor as separate downloads.

The Serial Monitor sits inside the editor window rather than in a window of its own, so you can keep several sketches open, each with its own monitor, to read what a board prints. Press Ctrl+T, or Cmd+T on a Mac, to tidy your code, and add a .clang-format file to set the style you like. For Wi-Fi boards such as the Nano 33 IoT or the UNO WiFi Rev 2, built-in tools update the Wi-Fi firmware and load SSL root certificates.

points.title: Version 2 is a real update over 1.x
points.text: IDE 2 has a reworked interface, better board and library managers, code autocomplete, a serial plotter and a debugger. Behind it, the Arduino CLI does the compiling and uploading, so builds match what the command-line tool would do.

points.title: The debugger needs specific hardware
points.text: Step-by-step debugging works with SAMD boards such as the Zero, Nano 33 IoT and the MKR family. Apart from the Zero, you also need a probe such as a Segger J-Link or Atmel-ICE. An Uno cannot be debugged this way.

points.title: Cloud sync is optional and free
points.text: With an Arduino account you can pull sketches from the Arduino Cloud, edit them offline and push them back. The feature itself costs nothing, but your Arduino Cloud plan's limits still apply. Without an account, sketches simply stay on your computer.

points.title: Needs a 64-bit system
points.text: IDE 2 runs on 64-bit Windows 10 or newer, macOS 10.15 Catalina or newer, and 64-bit Linux. If you are stuck on Windows 7 or 8, the legacy 1.8.19 release is still offered on Arduino's download page.

points.title: Linux: official AppImage, community Flatpak
points.text: Arduino's own Linux download is an x86-64 AppImage, which may need FUSE (`libfuse2` on Ubuntu 22.04 and later). The Flatpak listed here is a Flathub package that Flathub does not mark as verified. Either way, a udev rule may be needed before uploads reach the board.

points.title: Three ways to install on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 15 versions, each with an .exe installer, a machine-wide MSI and a zip you can run without installing. macOS has Intel and Apple Silicon builds, but macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.

points.title: Open source under AGPL
points.text: The IDE is licensed under the GNU AGPL v3 and built on the Eclipse Theia framework with Electron. It costs nothing to download and use.
